# Private N16 concurrent accepted-work control

The same framework-dependent AppSurface deployment supplies the privileged C#
supervisor and its nonroot worker. The compile-owned `EvidencePrivateQualification=N16`
image sends a fixed authenticated workload request, retains it while its accepted
body is blocked, and uses separate authenticated STOP and WAIT requests to join
that body. Ordinary builds retain `None` and cannot invoke this private control.

## Invocation and ownership

The workflow builds the pinned source and dependency graph with SDK 10.0.401,
then copies the framework-dependent payload and runtime 10.0.12 into protected
root-owned directories. `run-native.py` drives the fixed acquisition, source/ELF
inspection, root fixture and private retention sequence under original cumulative
deadlines. It supplies no caller-selected operation, process argument, admission
callback or producer registration. The root fixture observes the actual original
root process terminal, generated worker/owner units and cgroups, output bytes,
workspace, and named/reverse account deletion. Failure quarantines the owned paths.

The five stderr frames contain accepted-work data, kernel output data, the
original fixed failure, a final cleanup record, and the unchanged full ASEVD410
message. The actual Unix root exit remains 1. Parser success is diagnostic data;
original process settlement, immutable source/build/runtime/OS bindings, complete
EOF/quota checks and final root custody must also hold. No native result opens
Trusted eligibility or the production catalogue.

## Retained evidence

`retain-native.sh` selects fixed N16 paths only, preserves root-only regular
single-link files through identity and digest checks, and emits bounded canonical
USTAR. Root stdout must be empty; stderr is limited to 114688 bytes. Summary and
fixture-result records are limited to 4096 bytes, the request to 65536 bytes, and
the two full-path request/policy checksum rows to 4096 bytes. Both rows must bind
the exact retained request and the fixed fixture policy, in their original order.
The existing 32 MiB aggregate bound and cumulative
30-second retention deadline remain unchanged. Raw bytes are never public output.

The [runner](run-native.py) attempts [retention](retain-native.sh) after every
fixture dispatch outcome. Diagnostic collection cannot replace the original
failed outcome. Receipt publication also fails closed when writing, printing or
the original deadline fails; a successful fixture without a published receipt
cannot return success.

## Preparation paths and API contracts

The root bootstrap retains the reviewed [acquisition script](acquire-inbound.sh),
[transport script](prepare-root-inputs-v2.sh), fixture and parser plus the source
capture before privileged interpretation. The source capture has its own 2 MiB
bound; ordinary reviewed scripts retain the 128 KiB bound. Acquisition reads the
fixed `capture-receipt.json` directly from that protected bootstrap directory.

Acquisition creates the root-owned inbound tree. Transport accepts
`--source-commit` and copies its control records and scripts into a separate
protected input tree. The runner supplies every option exactly once. The
unprivileged [OS dependency audit](prepare-os-audit-v2.py) and the root
[fixture](checkpoint-n16-accepted-work.sh) use the transported input tree, with
root-only control data and sealed deployment directories. A fixed, empty,
root-owned `empty-audit-helper` directory satisfies the existing audit inventory
API. It contains no helper image, executable or workload.

The build receipt distinguishes the captured source's parent from the installed
harness's parent: the harness is a direct child of the captured source. The
runner and root scripts must preserve that distinction when comparing their
receipts. The fixture observation's five NSS checks are an integer count, not a
boolean. Its root projection is the actual build receipt digest. The detached
[record parser](check_n16_records.py) is interpreted only from retained bytes
whose digest matches the reviewed parser.

## Current preparation status

The source capture, C# source changes, fixture and parser have independent source
reviews. The local C# validation passed 452 focused tests; 21 portable parser
controls passed. The component integration has source reviews and focused portable controls.
Final installation and publisher review remain required before dispatch. Neither local evidence nor this preparation establishes
Linux N16 execution or product acceptance. Final native execution is mandatory.

## N16 v3 acquisition failure and v6 correction

The N16 v3 run failed during inbound acquisition before native dispatch: the parser
was copied to the same destination twice, and the second copy was rejected as a
copy collision. The v6 input removes only that duplicate list entry; the earlier
trusted pin and single mode-0444 copy remain. The source, fixture, deadlines,
custody rules and acceptance predicates are unchanged. The v6 installation review
is pending, and this preparation carries no native credit.
